basis.saw: the only content of the slide titled 'SPDX History' (the slide text is just that title); the timeline is the slide's whole substance

narrative.text: A timeline graphic headed 'Timeline of SPDX Evolution - Use Case by Use Case', with a 'MITRE' logo at the bottom left and the footer '(c) 2024 The MITRE Corporation. All rights reserved. Approved for Public Release; Distribution Unlimited. Case No: 23-01614-54'. A row of blue arrow segments carries years and versions: 2010 'SPDX begins', 2011 'SPDX 1.0', 2013 'SPDX 1.2', 2015 'SPDX 2.0', 2018 '2.1 to ISO', 2019, 2020, 2021 'SPDX 2.3', 2022, 2023 'SPDX 3rc1', 2024+ 'SPDX 3.0'. Below the arrows: 2010 'Standardized Single Package Information: Machine and human readable formats'; 2011 'Compliance Use Cases: Additional Project and License Information'; 2013 'Package Relations: 30+ additional use cases supported for complex packaging relationships and distribution scenarios'; 2015 'Security use cases: External references for vulnerabilities and product identification'; 2020 'SPDX & 3T-SBOM efforts merge: SPDX revises charter as an SDO'; 2021 'Free ISO Standard: ISO/IEC 5962 SPDX available' with a thumbnail of the 'ISO/IEC 5962:2021' cover; 2022 'Format Interoperability' with CDx and SPDX logos; 2023 'Profiles: New areas of use cases: Build, Data, Security, AI, Lite'; 2024+ 'Profiles: New areas of use cases: Services, Hardware, Safety'. Above the arrows: an 'I AM THE Cavalry' logo with 'Legislation: proposed software transparency, updatability & bill of material as reqts in safety critical sectors (automotive & healthcare)'; the NTIA seal with 'NTIA: Software Transparency begins'; OMG and CISQ logos with '3T-SBOM: OMG/CISQ begins w/ CONOPs for Tool-to-Tool SBOM'; two vertical labels 'SPDX 3.0 initial draft' and '3T-SBOM initial draft' at 2020; a seal with 'Transition of SBOM work to DHS'; a thumbnail of 'Executive Order on Improving the Nation's Cybersecurity' with 'Executive Order 14028'; and a document thumbnail with 'EU Cyber Resilience Act'.

basis.saw: the class diagram on the slide titled 'SPDX 3.1 Core', whose text lists the Core elements and cites 'https://github.com/spdx/spdx-3-model/blob/develop/images/model-Core.png'; the diagram is the slide's main content

narrative.text: UML class diagram in a frame tabbed 'Core profile', reproduced small: most attribute text is not legible at the extracted resolution, so only the larger class names are transcribed here, as drawn. Upper half: PhysicalLocation (attributes including country, countryCode, city, postalCode, postOfficeBoxNumber, provinceStateCode, streetAddress, geographicPointLocation), Location (locationTime), Requirement, Person, Organization (headquartersLocation : Location), SoftwareAgent and Agent; Element at the centre, with Annotation, Relationship, ElementCollection, SpdxDocument, Bundle, Bom, IndividualElement and LifecycleScopedRelationship around it; Tool and Artifact; DefinedProcess (processVersion, processRationale, processReadiness : ProcessReadinessType); Regulation pointing to Specification; and Action (actionStartTime, actionEndTime, actionLocation : Location, additionalInformation). Specification and Action each carry one attribute row shaded red. A 'Non-Element Classes' frame holds CreationInfo, ExternalIdentifier, ExternalMap, DictionaryEntry, ExternalRef, PositiveIntegerRange, NamespaceMap, IntegrityMethod with Hash and PackageVerificationCode, UnitOfMeasure (quantity, unitQUDT) with MeasureOfMass and MeasureOfLength, DefinedType and RequirementContext. A 'Simple Data Types' frame lists DateTime, MediaType, SemVer and one further type, and an 'Enumerations' frame lists about twelve enumeration names that are not reliably legible at this size.

basis.saw: the class diagram on the slide titled 'Hardware Profile', whose text lists Physical, Virtual and Bulk hardware and cites 'https://github.com/spdx/spdx-3-model/blob/develop/images/model-Hardware.png'

narrative.text: UML class diagram in a frame tabbed 'Hardware profile'. Above the frame sit Core/ Specification and Core/ Element. ProductSpecification (hazard: DefinedType [0..*]) specialises Core/Specification. The abstract Hardware specialises Core/Element, with productAgent :Agent [1], hardwareVersion:xsd:string [0..1], partNumber : xsd:string [1], releaseDate :DateTime [0..1], serialNumber : xsd:string [0..1], batchNumber : xsd:string [0..1], hazard: DefinedType [0..*], category: DefinedType [0..*], additionalInformationSpecification : /Core/Specification [0..*] and additionalInformation :/Core/DictionaryEntry [0..*]. Three classes specialise Hardware: PhysicalHardware (massOfHardware: MeasureOfMass [0..1], dimensions : Dimensions [0..1], centerOfMass : Dimensions [0..1]); BulkHardware (bulkQuantity :Core/UnitofMeasure, plus two rows shaded red: /Hardware/Hardware/serialNumber : xsd:string [0] and /Core/Element/description :xsd:string [1]); and VirtualHardware (virtualHardwareModel: VirtualHardwareModelType [0..1]). A separate Dimensions class has xAxisLength, yAxisLength and zAxisLength, each : MeasureOfLength [1], and an 'Enumerations' frame holds VirtualHardwareModelType.

basis.saw: the class diagram on the slide titled 'Supply Chain Profile', whose text lists Creation, Modify, Destroy, Actions, Responsibility, Use and Processes and cites 'https://github.com/spdx/spdx-3-model/blob/develop/images/model-SupplyChain.png'

narrative.text: UML class diagram of the Supply Chain profile, reproduced small: class names are mostly legible but most attribute text is not, so names are given as drawn and approximately. Three parents sit above the frame: Core/ Action, Core/ Artifact and Core/ DefinedProcess. The left column hangs action classes from Core/Action: CreateAction with HarvestingAction (or similar), AssemblyAction, ManufactureAction and ReproduceAction beneath it; UseAction with BoundaryCrossingAction, InspectionAction, OutOfSpecAction, PlanAction, ResolutionAction, a state-related action and TestAction; ModifyAction with ChangeAction, StorageAction and TransportAction; then BoundaryDefinitionAction, DestroyAction and ResponsibilityChangeAction. The right column mirrors it with process classes from Core/DefinedProcess: CreateProcess with InstantiateVirtualHardwareProcess, HarvestProcess, AssemblyProcess, ManufactureProcess and ReproduceProcess; UseProcess with InspectionProcess, PlanProcess, DefinedStateProcess and TestProcess among others; ModifyProcess with ChangeProcess, StorageProcess and TransportProcess; then BoundaryDefinitionProcess, DestroyProcess and ResponsibilityChangeProcess. A single class near the top centre hangs from Core/Artifact. Many classes carry one or more attribute rows shaded red, and a small 'Enumerations' frame at the lower right holds one enumeration.
